2ff33390-23dc-4880-948e-8ee3bd2f11da.text: "Of the following vice-presidential candidates, whom do you prefer?"

38019120-e014-411b-a000-9c5ca030c92d.text: Per CNC's May 19 survey, Petro has the lead in most runoff scenarios. Hernández is the only one who holds him to a stalemate.

418ce02f-f6a0-4251-a4de-bbd4d462c5b2.text: "If the elections were on Sunday, which of the following candidates would you vote for?"

data: Of men said they plan to vote for Petro, almost 10% higher than the percentage of women who do (36.6%).
Of voters age 18 to 25 who say they will vote for Petro. His support goes down as voters get older. Gutiérrez's support goes up, peaking at 34.1% among voters 56 and older.

Sources: Cifras y Conceptos was conducted March 30 – April 6, with a sample size of 1,843 and a ±3.7% margin of error. 

CNC May 19 was conducted from May 13 – 19, with a sample size of 4,412 and a ±1.5% margin of error. CNC May 13 was conducted from May 2 – 13, with a sample size of 6,204 and a ±1.2 margin of error. CNC April 21 was conducted from April 18 – 21, with a sample size of 4,159 and a ±1.4 margin of error.  CNC April 7 was conducted from April 4 – 7, with a sample size of 1,965 and a ±2.2 margin of error.  CNC March 31 was conducted from March 28 – 31, with a sample size of 4,206 and a ±1.5 margin of error.  CNC March 19 was conducted from March 18 – 19, with a sample size of 2,143 and a ±2.1 margin of error. La Silla Vacía includes polls from Invamer, CNC, Guarumo, YanHaas, Cifras y Conceptos, Datexco, Celag, Atlas, Massive Caller, and Medialab App and includes data from up to May 10.

data: Thought there was fraud in the March 13 elections.

6b96b362-f0c8-4b12-95fd-2081e1325e90.text: Colombians head to the polls on May 29 for the first presidential round. If no candidate receives over 50 percent of the votes cast, a runoff between the top two candidates will take place June 19.

705fa7b9-9a59-4364-9699-5534468605da.text: This data is based on the May 19 CNC polling. Sample size as follows: Antioquia and Eje Cafetero (648), Bogotá (437), Caribbean (806), Pacific (633), Center-East (843), and Center-South (493).
